name: Fertiliser supply
value: Hormuz closed to Gulf urea exports
summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind a largely closed Hormuz; tankers hit on 5 Nov
state: Hormuz, a route for about a third of world urea exports, remains largely closed in the conflict's ninth month, keeping fertiliser costs high (Global Agriculture; European Commission). Tankers were hit in the strait again on 5 Nov (US News). A key export route closed meets the Alert line.
for_you: Farmers face higher input costs, which can feed into food prices next season.

sources.title: Global Agriculture — Fertiliser costs stay high as Hormuz conflict drags into ninth month
European Commission — Fertilizer prices surge as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies
US News — Tankers hit in Hormuz

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
